# Copilot Instructions
- Project goal: automate downloads from UNIVESP-linked digital libraries (Pearson, Minha Biblioteca, Evolution) via PhantomJS + Bash; current state is paused/partial.
- Entrypoints: [UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher.sh](../UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher.sh) drives the CLI loop over a book list and dispatches PhantomJS login in [UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher.js](../UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher.js) which injects [header.js](../header.js) and the login flow in [login/loginUNIVESP.js](../login/loginUNIVESP.js).
- Config files: [conf/login](../conf/login) should contain username/password variables sourced by [header.sh](../header.sh); [conf/README.md](../conf/README.md) describes the login and list formats; book lists are pipe-delimited `LINK|AUTHOR|TÍTULO` passed as the script argument.
- Library detection: the shell wrapper checks the link for substrings (`univesp.bv3.digitalpages.com.br` → pearson, `integrada.minhabiblioteca.com.br` → mylib, `evolution.com.br` → evolution) before calling PhantomJS; unknown patterns exit with error map defined in [constants/errors.sh](../constants/errors.sh).
- Login behavior: `setLibrary` in [login/loginUNIVESP.js](../login/loginUNIVESP.js) drives SAML flows per provider with chained `setTimeout` waits; a title check gates success and non-success exits with code 2 (incorrect login) or 3 (unknown library). No retry/backoff is implemented, so keep timeouts generous when adding flows.
- Main limitation: [header.js](../header.js) references a missing `page/pages.js`, so post-login page scraping is not wired in the main script. The example fetchers contain the working download logic.
- Pearson example pipeline: [examples/PearsonFetcher/pearsonfetcher.sh](../examples/PearsonFetcher/pearsonfetcher.sh) reads the list, resolves first/last page via [info/page.sh](../examples/PearsonFetcher/info/page.sh) using PhantomJS probes ([info/fetchcover.js](../examples/PearsonFetcher/info/fetchcover.js), [info/fetchlast.js](../examples/PearsonFetcher/info/fetchlast.js)), downloads page images two at a time with [imgs/images.sh](../examples/PearsonFetcher/imgs/images.sh) + [imgs/fetchpdf.js](../examples/PearsonFetcher/imgs/fetchpdf.js), then builds the PDF with [book/pdfit.sh](../examples/PearsonFetcher/book/pdfit.sh). A `_`-prefixed first page is treated as BUG-1 and skipped into `failist`.
- Minha Biblioteca example pipeline: [examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/minhabibliotecafetcher.sh](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/minhabibliotecafetcher.sh) estimates the last page via [info/page.sh](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/info/page.sh) (calls `phantomjs check.js`), downloads images starting at page 193 with [imgs/image.sh](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/imgs/image.sh) using [imgs/fetchimg.js](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/imgs/fetchimg.js) and [imgs/downloadimg.js](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/imgs/downloadimg.js), then assembles PDFs with [imgs/book/pdfit.sh](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/imgs/book/pdfit.sh). Note: [info/check.js](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/info/check.js) currently contains an img2pdf shell script, so the last-page probe is broken and needs implementation.
- Cookies: both example fetchers rely on manual session cookies in [examples/PearsonFetcher/cookie.js](../examples/PearsonFetcher/cookie.js) and [examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/cookie.js](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/cookie.js); fill these locally, never commit real cookies or credentials.
- Dependencies: PhantomJS runtime, Bash, `wget`, `img2pdf`; timeouts are hard-coded (5–10s). When adding steps, stay consistent with PhantomJS idioms (`page.evaluate`, delayed `phantom.exit`) and keep viewport/clipRect in sync with target resolution.
- Error handling is minimal; exit codes bubble from PhantomJS (2 bad login, 3 unknown lib) and Bash uses an `error` array for user messaging. No retries or cleanup beyond temp image removal; preserve this behavior unless explicitly changing UX.
- Outputs: PDFs named `AUTHOR - TITLE.pdf` in `book/` for Pearson or in the repo root for the MB example; intermediate image folders are deleted after conversion.
- Security: do not embed secrets in tracked files; prefer sourcing from `conf/login` or local cookie stubs. Avoid logging full URLs with tokens.
- Known gaps for contributors: missing `page/pages.js` (main pipeline stops after login), broken MB last-page probe (`info/check.js`), and hard-coded page start offset 193 in [imgs/image.sh](../examples/MinhaBibliotecaFetcher/imgs/image.sh) likely library-specific.
- Suggested dev workflow: prototype changes inside `examples/*Fetcher` first (they contain the full flow), then backport stable pieces into the main `UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher` scripts; keep CLI signature (`./UNIVESPUniversalLibraryFetcher.sh <list>`) stable for users following [README.md](../README.md).
- Testing: run fetchers against a short list file with dummy cookies to verify page detection; validate generated PDFs and ensure temp folders are removed.
